newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN FASTEST FOR DUTCH GP.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN FASTEST FOR DUTCH GP.

text.p: World champion Michael Doohan of Australia overcame an early challenge by Spaniard Carlos Checa on Friday to qualify fastest for Saturday's Dutch 500cc Grand Prix.
The Honda rider clocked two minutes 2.512 seconds on the 6.05-km track, just outside the track record of 2:02.433 set by American Kevin Schwantz in 1991.
Italian Aprilia rider Doriano Romboni was second fastest in 2:02.884 ahead of Checa on a Honda.

"Things worked out okay in the end, although we did get caught out by the rain a bit because I had to start the session running-in a new engine," said Doohan, who has won the past three races in Assen.
"The bike is okay and the biggest thing is going to be the weather."
After a few minutes into the session Checa pipped Doohan at the top of the times list and looked likely to retain the position as rain started to fall.
But with some 20 minutes to go the rain stopped and Doohan regained the initiative on a dry track.

Doohan leads the championship with 145 points, 53 points clear of his Spanish teammate Alex Criville, who suffered severe injuries to his wrist and hand during a high speed crash in Thursday's qualifying session.
Criville, who won here in 1992, had a successful operation after the 240 kph crash, a medical statement said.
He will miss the next race at Imola on July 6 but might be fit for the German Grand Prix two weeks later.
